title: Apollo.io Review (2026)
intro: Apollo.io is a sales intelligence and engagement platform that combines B2B contact data, prospecting, sequences, enrichment, and lightweight deals. This review covers Free/Basic/Professional/Enterprise pricing, capabilities, and CRM fit.
summary: Apollo is strongest for outbound data + engagement, not as a pure pipeline CRM. Basic starts at $49/mo; Professional at $99/mo; Enterprise is custom. Scores reflect first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
verdict: Apollo.io is a strong sales intelligence and engagement platform for outbound teams that need B2B data, sequencing, and enrichment — with only secondary deal/pipeline CRM depth. Basic ($49) and Professional ($99) are the published paid rungs; Enterprise is custom. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research — not hands-on product testing.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Apollo packages prospecting and engagement in one GTM workspace; powerful, but credit/seat concepts add learning curve versus simple CRMs.
Deals tracking exists, yet Apollo’s center of gravity is data + engagement — pipeline CRM depth is secondary versus Pipedrive-style tools.
Sequences, engagement automation, and AI-assisted outbound workflows are core documented strengths on paid plans.
Multichannel engagement and email sequencing are first-class; this is an engagement platform more than a marketing ESP.
GTM analytics and engagement reporting are part of the product story for paid teams coaching outbound performance.
Useful for outbound plays and workflows, but not positioned as a deeply configurable CRM admin platform.
CRM syncs (e.g., Salesforce/HubSpot style connectors) and API/custom plan access are documented for stack-heavy teams.
Credits, fair-use, seats, and record-selection limits create ongoing ops work versus flat simple CRM plans.
Professional and custom Enterprise packaging target growing GTM orgs with governance and API needs.
Free plan plus Basic at $49 can be strong for outbound teams that will use data/credits; pure CRM buyers may overpay for the wrong center of gravity.

faq.question: How much does Apollo.io cost?
faq.answer: Apollo’s pricing page publishes Free ($0), Basic ($49/month), Professional ($99/month), and Enterprise (contact sales) in USD schema.org offers. Credits and fair-use rules also affect total cost — confirm on Apollo’s site.

faq.question: Is Apollo a CRM?
faq.answer: Apollo includes deals/pipeline-style tracking, but it is primarily a sales intelligence and engagement platform. Buyers needing pipeline-first CRM should compare dedicated CRMs.

faq.question: Does Apollo have a free plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Apollo documents a Free plan with core free features and limited data access.

faq.question: Is this a hands-on SoftwareGlimpse lab review?
faq.answer: No. This review is approved based on first-party Apollo pricing and product research, not hands-on testing.

sections.heading: What Apollo is
sections.body: Apollo.io combines B2B data, prospecting, enrichment, and engagement sequences. Deals exist, but the product is built for go-to-market execution more than classic CRM administration.

sections.heading: Pricing and plans
sections.body: Published offers are Free, Basic ($49/mo), Professional ($99/mo), and Enterprise (custom). Total cost depends on seats plus credits/fair-use consumption.

sections.heading: Core capabilities
sections.body: Documented strengths include prospecting, enrichment, sequences, AI insights, integrations, and secondary deals tracking.

sections.heading: Who it’s for
sections.body: Best for outbound/GTM teams. Less ideal as a sole pipeline CRM for teams that only need deal boards.

productExperience.summary: Based on Apollo’s documented workflow, teams find accounts/contacts, enrich records, run multichannel sequences, track engagement, and optionally manage deals — with AI insights layered onto GTM motions.
